summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diastolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for acute respiratory distress due to fluid overload from acute-on-chronic diastolic heart failure. She presented with severe hypertension and pulmonary edema, requiring emergent hemodialysis with removal of approximately 3 liters of fluid. A central line was placed in the left femoral vein due to difficult IV access, later removed without complication. Her symptoms improved rapidly post-dialysis, and she was weaned off respiratory support. A urinary tract infection with Enterococcus was identified and treated with levofloxacin, while infectious workup for pneumonia was negative. She remained hemodynamically stable with normal cardiac enzymes and was discharged home on her baseline medications with adjustments to warfarin dosing and instructions to complete a short course of antibiotics and monitor INR closely.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
